'''Herbert Whittier Jones''' (31 January 1927 - 2 October 2002) was an American physicist and longtime professor at [[Florida A&M University]]. He was known for his research in developing methods for the evaluation of overlap and Coulomb integrals over [[Slater-type orbital|Slater-type orbitals]] (STOs) for molecular calculations.<ref name=":0">{{cite journal |last1=Hoggan |first1=Philip E. |last2=Weatherford |first2=Charles A. |title=In memory of Herbert W. Jones (1927-2002) |journal=International Journal of Quantum Chemistry |date=2004 |volume=100 |issue=2 |pages=67–68 |doi=10.1002/qua.20106 |doi-access=free}}</ref> He is credited as a founder of the Florida A&M University physics department.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news |date=17 April 2009 |title=FAMU to host Jones memorial seminar |pages=5 |work=[[Tallahassee Democrat]]}}</ref> 

==Early life and education==
Jones was born in 1927 in [[Chicago|Chicago, Illinois]], to John and Ada V. Jones.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Herbert Jones Obituary (2002) - Tallahassee, FL - Tallahassee Democrat |url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/tallahassee/name/herbert-jones-obituary?id=28068816 |access-date=2023-03-14 |website=Legacy.com}}</ref> He served in the Navy during World War II.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Roberson |first=Stephen |date=16 February 2023 |title=Florida A&M University Department of Physics |url=https://nsbp.org/blogpost/2063847/Black-History-Month-2023 |access-date=16 March 2023 |website=National Society of Black Physicists}}</ref> 

He received his bachelor's degree in 1949 from the [[College of Liberal Arts and Sciences (University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign)|College of Liberal Arts and Sciences]] at the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]], and graduated with honors in the physical sciences.<ref>{{Cite web |last=University of Illinois |date=12 June 1949 |title=University of Illinois Commencement Program |url=https://ia800202.us.archive.org/15/items/commencementprog19461951univ/commencementprog19461951univ.pdf |access-date=13 March 2023 |website=Archive.org}} ([https://web.archive.org/web/20220215151626/https://ia800202.us.archive.org/15/items/commencementprog19461951univ/commencementprog19461951univ.pdf archived version])</ref> He then completed his graduate studies at the [[Horace H. Rackham School of Graduate Studies]] at the [[University of Michigan]], graduating with a master's degree in physics in 1950<ref>{{Cite book |last=Michigan |first=University of |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HOueAAAAMAAJ&dq=%22herbert+whittier+jones%22&pg=RA2-PA48 |title=Commencement Programs |date=1948 |language=en}}</ref> and a PhD in physics in 1959. His thesis was titled "A Method of Obtaining and Analyzing Time-Resolved Intensity Patterns of the Radiation from Various Regions of a Vacuum Spark Discharge."<ref>{{Cite book |last=Regents |first=University of Michigan Board of |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Y6EqAQAAMAAJ&dq=%22herbert+whittier+jones%22&pg=PA1169 |title=Regents' Proceedings |date=1957 |publisher=The University |language=en}}</ref> His doctoral committee included W. Wallace McCormick, [[Charles L. Dolph]], [[Ralph A. Sawyer]], Marcellus Lee Wiedenbeck, and Ralph A. Wolfe.<ref>{{cite thesis |last1=Jones |first1=Herbert Whittier |date=1960 |title=A Method Of Obtaining And Analyzing Time-resolved Intensity Patterns Of The Radiation From Various Regions Of A Vacuum Spark Discharge |id={{ProQuest|301845396}} |bibcode=1960PhDT.........8J |oclc=77216189}}</ref>

At the [[University of Michigan]], he was a member of the [[Sigma Xi]] honor society,<ref>{{cite news |title=To Outstanding 'U' Students for Scholarship, Citizenship |newspaper=The Michigan Daily |volume=69 |issue=156 |date=8 May 1959 |url=https://digital.bentley.umich.edu/midaily/mdp.39015071754050/539}}</ref> [[Phi Beta Kappa]], and the [[Alpha Phi Alpha]] fraternity.<ref name=":1" />

==Career==
Jones was a professor of physics at [[Florida A&M University]] for 43 years, and served as chair of the physics department for 12 years.<ref name=":0" /> In 1976, he was also the head of the university's Division of Natural Sciences and Mathematics.<ref>{{Cite news |date=11 April 1976 |title=Minorities are gaining in sciences, FAMU hears |pages=2C |work=[[Tallahassee Democrat]]}}</ref>

During his time at [[Florida A&M University]], Jones led the Molecular Physics Project along with Charles Weatherford and Babu L. Jain. The project was supported by multiple [[NASA]] grants.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2 December 1979 |title=Career day set at TCC |pages=12C |work=[[Tallahassee Democrat]]}}</ref> From August 3-6, 1981, Jones and Weatherford hosted the first International Conference on ETO Multicenter Molecular Integrals in [[Tallahassee, Florida]]. The conference was sponsored by Florida A&M University's Institute for Molecular Computations and physics department, and involved 34 scientists from eight different countries. The proceedings were compiled into a 1981 book, "ETO Multicenter Molecular Integrals."<ref>{{cite book |doi=10.1007/978-94-009-7921-5 |title=ETO Multicenter Molecular Integrals |year=1982 |isbn=978-94-009-7923-9 |editor-last1=Weatherford |editor-last2=Jones |editor-first1=Charles A. |editor-first2=Herbert W.}}{{pn|date=April 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=7 January 1983 |title=This weekend's radio highlights |pages=9B |work=[[Tallahassee Democrat]]}}</ref>

In 1982, Jones spent a sabbatical period with the Quantum Theory Group at the [[Uppsala University|University of Uppsala]] in [[Uppsala|Uppsala, Sweden]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=28 February 1982 |title=Achievements |pages=3G |work=[[Tallahassee Democrat]]}}</ref>

==Research==
Jones "contributed greatly to the solution of the STO integral problem." He based his work on the [[Per-Olov Löwdin|Löwdin]] alpha functions, and with Charles Weatherford, made considerable progress in the development of the so-called C-matrix with all integer elements. His later research involved building a detector for [[Magnetic monopole|magnetic monopoles]].<ref name=":0" />

Between 1976 and 1995, with a grant from the [[United States Air Force|U.S. Air Force]], Jones developed a computer program in [[Fortran]] language to implement Slater-type orbital calculations digitally.<ref>{{Cite news |last=FAMU Office of Public Affairs |date=9 August 1995 |title=Physics professor on the math track |pages=5C |work=[[Tallahassee Democrat]]}}</ref>

==Awards and legacy==
In 2000, Jones was awarded the National Millennium Award for Research by the White House Initiative on Historically Black Colleges. [[Ronald E. Mickens]] was Jones' fellow honoree for this award.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2000-10-11 |title=White House Initiative Honors Science Faculty With Millennium Awards |url=https://www.diverseeducation.com/institutions/hbcus/article/15077212/white-house-initiative-honors-science-faculty-with-millennium-awards |access-date=2023-03-12 |website=Diverse: Issues In Higher Education |language=en-us}}</ref>

The Herbert W. Jones Endowed Scholarships at [[Florida A&M University]] are named for Jones and are awarded to undergraduate students in the college of science and technology.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Herbert W. Jones Endowed Scholarships - Florida A&M University Scholarships |url=https://famu.academicworks.com/opportunities/4355 |access-date=2023-03-12 |website=famu.academicworks.com}}</ref> In 2002, FAMU began hosting the annual Herbert W. Jones Memorial Seminar.<ref name=":2" />

==Personal life==
Jones was married to Gladys Hurt Jones, who he met at the [[University of Michigan]]. They had one daughter.<ref name=":1" />
